parsed.why: No criminalisation, constitutional equality reform, no documented targeting or traveler-facing restriction; but thin record, no trans-specific protection or acceptance evidence, dated stigma noted. Structural signals resolve moderately safe, not better.

Universal-exposure regime: passport sex-marker policy with detentions/stranding, visa fraud flagging, state facility bans with criminal exposure and an arrest, hostile custody practices, state threat-framing. Courts contest but do not remedy; state patchwork gives partial relief only.

Self-ID law, facility access by identity, gender-identity aggravation actually enforced (convictions, sentences), documented trans-supportive society and welcoming institutions; regional backlash is resident-facing and limited.

Decriminalised since 2014; no documented targeting, incidents or traveler-facing restriction. But no protections, no recognition, marriage ban, no documented trans acceptance and thin record — no exposures, no documented relief either.

State actors perpetrate: police raids, collective lesbian detentions, custody sexual violence, conversion rape, discriminatory instruments, 1954-law application, activist detention, impunity. Severe state-tolerated targeting dominates despite formal decriminalisation.
